newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnia launches watchdog agency for donor money.
newsitem.headline: Bosnia launches watchdog agency for donor money.

text.p: The Bosnian government announced on Wednesday it had joined the World Bank in setting up a watchdog agency to ensure international donor money was used properly.
The director of the World Bank mission in Sarajevo, Rory O'Sullivan, said the government was concerned that procurement should be carried out in a way that ensured best value for money for Bosnia.
An international donor conference in April in Brussels pledged $1.8 billion for Bosnia's post-war reconstruction, of which $550 million has been dispersed, O'Sullivan said.
"We expect this agency to play a major role and really give confidence to the donors that the funds are being used properly," he added.
The new agency comes after the U.S. special envoy in Bosnia, Richard Sklar, critisised the Bosnian government's ability to move forward with post-war economic reconstruction.

He said in a newspaper interview two weeks ago that donor money was arriving slowly not only because of bureaucratic procedures but also because of the "government's transfer of money to various accounts."
"The Bosnian government's first objective is not speeding up the process but directing funds to those companies it prefers, and also being too bureaucratic," Sklar said.
Bosnian Prime Minister Hasan Muratovic denied the charges and said Sklar appeared not to be familiar with government procedures.
Government officials present at the launch of the new agency said they had worked on the project for the last four months.
"This is a prevention of the things that may occur later," a foreign ministry official said.
O'Sullivan said that corruption had not been a concern for the World Bank in any of the reconstruction programme it had been involved in.
"We have absolutely no evidence that there has been any behaviour which could be called that," he said.

The agency will cooperate with a Dutch consulting company specialized in monitoring and auditing procurements during the first year of its existence and will also be funded by the Dutch government. Dutch experts are expected to arrive next month.
